front: How does RAGAS's Faithfulness metric work, mechanically?
back: It decomposes the generated answer into atomic claims via LLM decomposition, checks each claim individually against retrieved context, and scores supported claims ÷ total claims -- a graded signal instead of one binary answer-level judgment.

front: How does Answer Relevancy work, and how does it deliberately mirror HyDE?
back: It generates several hypothetical questions the answer would be a good response to, then compares those to the original question via embedding cosine similarity. It's the mirror image of HyDE -- comparing question-to-question instead of question-to-answer avoids the same phrasing-asymmetry problem HyDE fixes on the retrieval side.

front: What does Context Precision measure, and what does a low score with relevant chunks present indicate?
back: Whether the relevant chunks among those retrieved are ranked near the top (an LLM judges each chunk's relevance individually). A low score with genuinely-relevant chunks buried lower points at a reranking problem, not a recall problem.

front: What does Context Recall measure, and why is it the one metric needing ground truth?
back: Whether retrieval captured everything needed to answer correctly -- it decomposes the reference answer into claims and checks each against retrieved context (not the generated answer). It's the only one of the four core metrics that requires a ground-truth reference answer.

front: What were the four core RAGAS scores measured on the standard 8-question eval set?
back: Faithfulness 0.9062, Answer Relevancy 0.8596, Context Precision (with reference) 0.6250, Context Recall 0.8750.

front: In RAGAS's diagnostic table, what does High Faithfulness + High Answer Relevancy + Low Context Precision + High Context Recall indicate?
back: A reranking problem -- the right information was retrieved (high recall) but ranked poorly (low precision), while generation itself is fine.

front: In RAGAS's diagnostic table, what does High Faithfulness + High Answer Relevancy + Low Context Recall indicate?
back: A retrieval/indexing problem -- necessary information was never retrieved at all, even though generation handled what it did get correctly.

front: What was the page's real anomaly finding: a factually correct answer with near-zero grounding?
back: Asked for the English-to-German BLEU score, the pipeline answered correctly (28.4), but scored near-zero on faithfulness and context recall across separate runs -- the retrieved chunks never actually contained "28.4" (one was cut off, two covered the English-to-French numbers), meaning the model answered from parametric memory, not retrieved context.

front: Which of the four core RAGAS metrics can run without ground-truth reference answers?
back: Faithfulness, Answer Relevancy, and Context Precision -- all using only the question, retrieved context, and generated answer. Only Context Recall requires a ground-truth reference.

front: In the page's measured example, why did FactualCorrectness score 0.0 while SemanticSimilarity scored 0.877 on the same answer/reference pair?
back: FactualCorrectness's claim-decomposition-plus-NLI check is stricter about phrasing/scope (singular vs. plural framing, an added specific number) than embedding similarity -- a low FactualCorrectness score alone isn't proof of an actual factual error.

front: Why does ragas's multi-hop synthesizer fail to generate questions from a single paper?
back: Multi-hop generation needs genuine cross-document/cross-entity relationships to cluster on; a single technical paper doesn't have enough thematic overlap between its own sections, so every run falls back to single-hop synthesizers only.
